  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that when the Kohen Gadol enters the Holy of Holies to effect atonement, the revelation of the essential connection of the soul's essence with Atzmus is so transcendent that no angel or even those with human-like faces may be present, as in Atzmus Ein Sof there is no place for angels—only Israel and the King alone.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is “And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he comes to atone in the Holy,”</t>
    <t s="2">that this “no man shall be,” etc., even those whose faces are the faces of a man, is specifically when the Kohen Gadol comes into the Holy of Holies to atone in the Holy,</t>
    <t s="3">because the revelation that is above the chain of descent that was in the Holy of Holies in its own right,</t>
    <t s="4">has a connection to the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="5">and relative to this revelation there is a place for angels.</t>
    <t s="6">But when he comes</t>
    <t s="7">(of the Kohen Gadol into the Holy of Holies)</t>
    <t s="8">to atone in the Holy,</t>
    <t s="9">that is, that through the service of the Kohen Gadol in the Holy of Holies, atonement was drawn down for all of Israel, this is because through his service the connection of the essence of the soul with Atzmus is revealed,</t>
    <t s="10">for in the Atzmus of Ein Sof there is absolutely no place for angels,</t>
    <t s="11">Israel and the King alone,</t>
    <t s="12">therefore then “no man shall be,” even those whose faces are the faces of a man.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="16">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that in the Neilah prayer on Yom Kippur, the revelation of the Yechidah level of the soul shines even more than in the Musaf prayer, corresponding to the five levels of the soul, and it is called Neilah because all gates are locked and even the highest creations cannot enter—only Israel and the King alone.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to add,</t>
    <t s="1">that in the Neilah prayer this revelation shines even more than in the Musaf of Yom Kippur, in which the order of the service of the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur is recited.</t>
    <t s="2">For the five prayers of Yom Kippur correspond to the five levels of the soul,</t>
    <t s="3">Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="4">For the first three prayers are in Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah,</t>
    <t s="5">and the Musaf prayer of Yom Kippur is in Chayah,</t>
    <t s="6">and the revelation of Yechidah is</t>
    <t s="7">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="8">in the Neilah prayer.</t>
    <t s="9">And therefore it is called Neilah,</t>
    <t s="10">because then all the gates are locked, and even the highest creations</t>
    <t s="11">(and even emanations, etc.)</t>
    <t s="12">cannot enter,</t>
    <t s="13">Israel and the King alone.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="17">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the revelation of the essential connection of Atzmus with the essence of the soul to the verse about Yosef and his brothers, explaining that this is the meaning of Shemini Atzeret, where all the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are present but in a line of joy, and it is “for you alone, with no stranger with you.”</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is also what is said in the Zohar</t>
    <t s="1">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="2">“And no man stood with him when Yosef made himself known to his brothers,”</t>
    <t s="3">“At the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, unites with Israel,” etc. “Therefore on the day</t>
    <t s="4">of the eighth day, it shall be an assembly for you,”</t>
    <t s="5">for it can be said that the matter of “the Holy One, blessed be He, unites with Israel” is the revelation of the Yechidah and the essential connection of Atzmus with the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="6">[And it can be said that the connection of this matter to Yosef,</t>
    <t s="7">for the name Yosef is from “May Hashem add to me another son,”</t>
    <t s="8">that even “another” becomes a son,</t>
    <t s="9">because through the revelation of the essential connection of Atzmus in Israel</t>
    <t s="10">(“when Yosef made himself known to his brothers”)</t>
    <t s="11">it is revealed that even “another” is a son.]</t>
    <t s="12">And this revelation is on Shemini Atzeret,</t>
    <t s="13">and as is known, on Shemini Atzeret all the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are present,</t>
    <t s="14">except that on Shemini Atzeret they are in a line of joy,</t>
    <t s="15">and therefore “on the eighth day it shall be an assembly for you,”</t>
    <t s="16">“they shall be</t>
    <t s="17">for you alone, and no stranger with you.”</t>
  </section>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that when the Kohen Gadol enters the Holy of Holies to effect atonement, the revelation of the essential connection of the soul's essence with Atzmus is so transcendent that no angel or even those with human-like faces may be present, as in Atzmus Ein Sof there is no place for angels—only Israel and the King alone.

translations.translation: And this is “And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he comes to atone in the Holy,”
that this “no man shall be,” etc., even those whose faces are the faces of a man, is specifically when the Kohen Gadol comes into the Holy of Holies to atone in the Holy,
because the revelation that is above the chain of descent that was in the Holy of Holies in its own right,
has a connection to the chain of descent,
and relative to this revelation there is a place for angels.
But when he comes
(of the Kohen Gadol into the Holy of Holies)
to atone in the Holy,

that is, that through the service of the Kohen Gadol in the Holy of Holies, atonement was drawn down for all of Israel, this is because through his service the connection of the essence of the soul with Atzmus is revealed,
for in the Atzmus of Ein Sof there is absolutely no place for angels,
Israel and the King alone,
therefore then “no man shall be,” even those whose faces are the faces of a man.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the Neilah prayer on Yom Kippur, the revelation of the Yechidah level of the soul shines even more than in the Musaf prayer, corresponding to the five levels of the soul, and it is called Neilah because all gates are locked and even the highest creations cannot enter—only Israel and the King alone.

translations.translation: And to add,
that in the Neilah prayer this revelation shines even more than in the Musaf of Yom Kippur, in which the order of the service of the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur is recited.
For the five prayers of Yom Kippur correspond to the five levels of the soul,
Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah.
For the first three prayers are in Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah,
and the Musaf prayer of Yom Kippur is in Chayah,
and the revelation of Yechidah is
(primarily)
in the Neilah prayer.
And therefore it is called Neilah,
because then all the gates are locked, and even the highest creations
(and even emanations, etc.)
cannot enter,
Israel and the King alone.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the revelation of the essential connection of Atzmus with the essence of the soul to the verse about Yosef and his brothers, explaining that this is the meaning of Shemini Atzeret, where all the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are present but in a line of joy, and it is “for you alone, with no stranger with you.”

translations.translation: And this is also what is said in the Zohar
on the verse,
“And no man stood with him when Yosef made himself known to his brothers,”
“At the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, unites with Israel,” etc. “Therefore on the day
of the eighth day, it shall be an assembly for you,”
for it can be said that the matter of “the Holy One, blessed be He, unites with Israel” is the revelation of the Yechidah and the essential connection of Atzmus with the essence of the soul.
[And it can be said that the connection of this matter to Yosef,
for the name Yosef is from “May Hashem add to me another son,”
that even “another” becomes a son,
because through the revelation of the essential connection of Atzmus in Israel
(“when Yosef made himself known to his brothers”)
it is revealed that even “another” is a son.]
And this revelation is on Shemini Atzeret,
and as is known, on Shemini Atzeret all the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are present,
except that on Shemini Atzeret they are in a line of joy,
and therefore “on the eighth day it shall be an assembly for you,”
“they shall be
for you alone, and no stranger with you.”
